purpose: Measure deterministic Game Book/source-name compatibility inside same-season/week/team/jersey candidate sets for every V1 exact-name miss, after rejecting candidate uniqueness alone as unsafe.

rejected_design_preservation.reason: Diagnostic examples exposed semantically false unique candidates caused by jersey reuse and weekly roster snapshot mismatch.
examples: PHI K.Grugier-Hill #54 -> Stephen Tulloch / Deontae Skinner candidate set

population.population_rule: all and only V1 exact zero-candidate Game Book identities

compatibility_taxonomy.normalization: Unicode NFKD; uppercase alphanumeric compact forms; surname components preserve hyphen/space/apostrophe boundaries for component comparisons.

given_evidence.given_full_prefix: Game Book given fragment contains at least two alphanumeric characters and prefixes source first_name or football_name.
given_evidence.given_initial_only: Game Book given fragment contributes only a first-initial match; reported separately as weaker evidence.
given_evidence.given_absent: No usable given fragment; never counted as strong evidence.

surname_evidence.surname_exact: compact Game Book surname equals compact source last_name
surname_evidence.compound_component_prefix: Game Book and source surname component sequences have equal length and every Game Book component prefixes the corresponding source component
surname_evidence.source_surname_is_gamebook_leading_compo: source surname component sequence equals a leading sequence of the Game Book surname components
surname_evidence.gamebook_surname_is_source_leading_compo: Game Book surname component sequence equals a leading sequence of the source surname components
surname_evidence.surname_absent: no usable Game Book surname fragment

strong_tier: given_initial_only + compound_component_prefix when a nontrivial surname component supplies distinguishing evidence
